dedupe_keys.name: gathering spaces in recovery after the 2011 great east japan earthquake and tsunami

description: Disasters destroy gathering and public spaces along with infrastructure and houses, weakening community ties. This study compared how community participation in government-led and community-driven recovery after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami shaped the gathering spaces that were rebuilt, using Arnstein's ladder of citizen participation and Henri Lefebvre's production of space as theory, and case studies with interviews and questionnaire surveys as evidence. Coverage: selected recovery areas in the tsunami-affected region. Access: open-access article in City, Territory and Architecture (2023), with a PubMed Central copy. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: a small number of cases and qualitative evidence. Outcome: community-driven cases produced small, evenly superimposed, accessible and diverse open spaces that served users well; government-led cases produced centralised spaces near disaster public housing whose primary and secondary spaces lacked connections. Simulation uses: representing public-space provision and access in community recovery models. Related records: the Christchurch post-earthquake placemaking case and the Nepal housing non-recovery study.
